subtopic: Scenario programming tasks
stem:
Pre-release style scenario (practise as if you had programmed it beforehand):
A cricket academy in Sialkot measures the speed of every delivery in km/h at a fast-bowling camp. There are 8 bowlers and each bowls 6 deliveries.
Task 1 – store the names of the 8 bowlers, then input the 6 speeds for each bowler. A speed is valid only if it is from 60 to 160 km/h.
Task 2 – calculate and output each bowler's name and average speed, rounded to one decimal place.
Task 3 – find and output the fastest single delivery of the camp and the name of the bowler who bowled it.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write pseudocode to declare the arrays needed for Task 1. Use BowlerName to store the 8 names and Speed to store the 6 speeds of each bowler.
parts.answer:
DECLARE BowlerName : ARRAY[1:8] OF STRING
DECLARE Speed : ARRAY[1:8, 1:6] OF REAL
parts.working: 1 mark: BowlerName as a 1D array of 8 strings. 1 mark: Speed as a 2D array 8 × 6 of REAL.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write pseudocode for the part of Task 1 that inputs and validates one speed and stores it in Speed[B, D], where B is the bowler number and D the delivery number.
parts.answer:
OUTPUT "Enter speed in km/h"
INPUT S
WHILE S < 60 OR S > 160 DO
    OUTPUT "Invalid – speed must be from 60 to 160"
    INPUT S
ENDWHILE
Speed[B, D] ← S
parts.working: 1 mark: prompt and input. 1 mark: loop with the correct range check (< 60 OR > 160) and an error message with re-input. 1 mark: valid value stored in Speed[B, D].

parts.label: c
parts.text: State which of these inputs your validation would reject: 58, 60, 160, 172.5
parts.working: 1 mark for both values and no others (60 and 160 are boundary values that are accepted).

parts.label: d
parts.text: In Task 2, Usman's six speeds are 132.4, 138.0, 141.6, 129.9, 135.2 and 137.5. Calculate his average speed, rounded to one decimal place.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Explain how your program would carry out Task 3.
parts.answer: Set Fastest to the first speed, Speed[1, 1], and FastBowler to 1. Use nested loops to visit every bowler (1 to 8) and every delivery (1 to 6). If Speed[B, D] is greater than Fastest, store it in Fastest and store B in FastBowler. After the loops output BowlerName[FastBowler] and Fastest.
parts.working: 1 mark: initialise the highest value (first element or 0) with a variable for the bowler. 1 mark: nested loops through all 48 speeds comparing each with the highest so far and updating both variables. 1 mark: output the name (using the stored index) and the speed.

subtopic: Scenario programming tasks
stem:
Pre-release style scenario (practise as if you had programmed it beforehand):
A coach company runs three trips a day from Lahore to Islamabad, leaving at 07:00, 13:00 and 19:00 (departures 1, 2 and 3). Each coach has 40 seats.
Task 1 – set up an array SeatsLeft[1:3] with every value set to 40, and set the day's takings to 0.
Task 2 – for a booking, input the departure (1 to 3) and the number of adult and child passengers. An adult ticket costs Rs 2800 and a child ticket Rs 1400. A group of 6 or more passengers gets 10% off the total cost. Refuse the booking if there are not enough seats left. Otherwise output the cost, update the seats left and add the cost to the takings.
Task 3 – at the end of the day, output the total takings and the departure time that carried the most passengers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an algorithm in pseudocode for Task 2. Assume the array SeatsLeft[1:3] and a REAL variable Takings have already been set up in Task 1.
parts.answer:
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Departure (1, 2 or 3)"
    INPUT Dep
UNTIL Dep >= 1 AND Dep <= 3
OUTPUT "Number of adults"
INPUT Adults
OUTPUT "Number of children"
INPUT Children
Total ← Adults + Children
IF Total < 1 OR Total > SeatsLeft[Dep] THEN
    OUTPUT "Booking not possible – seats left: ", SeatsLeft[Dep]
ELSE
    Cost ← Adults * 2800 + Children * 1400
    IF Total >= 6 THEN
        Cost ← Cost * 0.9
    ENDIF
    SeatsLeft[Dep] ← SeatsLeft[Dep] - Total
    Takings ← Takings + Cost
    OUTPUT "Cost: Rs ", Cost
ENDIF
parts.working: 1 mark each for: input and validation of the departure (1 to 3); input of adults and children with total calculated; check that 1 ≤ total ≤ seats left, with a message if not; cost = adults × 2800 + children × 1400; 10% discount only when total ≥ 6; seats left reduced and takings increased, with cost output.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A family books 4 adult and 3 child tickets on one departure. Calculate the cost of the booking. Show your working.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A departure has 9 seats left. Give one normal, one boundary and one erroneous value to test the total number of passengers in a booking, and state the expected result of each.
parts.answer:
Normal: 4 – booking accepted.
Boundary: 9 – booking accepted (the largest group that fits; 10 would be rejected).
Erroneous: 15 (or −2, or "two") – booking rejected with an error message.
parts.working: 1 mark each: a normal value between 1 and 9 with 'accepted'; a boundary value (9 or 1 accepted, or 10 / 0 rejected) with the correct result; an erroneous value (well outside the range or wrong type) with 'rejected'.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain how Task 3 can find the departure with the most passengers, using SeatsLeft.
parts.answer: For each departure the passengers carried = 40 − SeatsLeft[d]. Set Most to the passengers on departure 1 and BestDep to 1, then loop through departures 2 to 3; if a departure's passengers is greater than Most, update Most and BestDep. Finally output the departure time for BestDep and Most.
parts.working: 1 mark: passengers calculated as 40 − SeatsLeft (or the smallest SeatsLeft used). 1 mark: loop comparing each departure with the highest so far and storing which departure it is. 1 mark: output of the departure and the number of passengers (with total takings).
